chunks: Abu Ahmad al-Hasan ibn Abdullah ibn Sa'id al-Askari narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Qushayri narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Huwaysh Ahmad ibn Isa al-Kufi narrated to us, saying: Musa ibn Isma'il ibn Musa ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from his grandfather Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his grandfather, from Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them).
Regarding the saying of Allah, Exalted and Mighty: 'And do not forget your share of the world.'
He said: Do not forget your health, strength, free time, youth, and vitality, [by] seeking the Hereafter through them.
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'do not forget your share of the world' in Shia interpretation?
ai.summary: In *Ma'ani al-Akhbar*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this interpretation from the Imams, linking the Quranic command to balance worldly vitality with spiritual pursuit. It clarifies that 'not forgetting' one's share means actively leveraging youth, health, and energy as capital for the Hereafter, rather than neglecting the world entirely or becoming overly attached to it.
